members: [untitled BTM module] These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the mature myeloid compartment, particularly monocytes, macrophages and neutrophils, and the secretory and degradative capabilities that make those cells useful in innate immunity and tissue remodelling. Surface ectoenzymes such as aminopeptidase N and maltase-glucoamylase digest peptides and carbohydrates at the plasma membrane, an aquaglyceroporin channel moves water and small solutes during phagocyte activation and swelling, and a secreted sulfatase edits heparan sulfate on the extracellular matrix to release bound growth factors and chemokines.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the interface between proliferative arrest and inflammatory secretion that characterises cellular senescence. On the chromatin side, the Polycomb component BMI1 is part of the complex that ubiquitinates histone H2A to silence the CDKN2A locus and keep cells cycling, while the deubiquitinase USP16 removes that mark and opposes it, so the balance between them sets how readily a cell exits the cycle.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on transcriptional repression and chromatin-based silencing, the machinery that keeps developmental and proliferative genes switched off until they are needed. Polycomb components are the anchor: BMI1 is a core subunit of the PRC1 ubiquitin ligase complex that marks histone H2A to maintain silencing, while AEBP2 is a zinc-finger accessory factor that helps target the companion PRC2 methyltransferase to chromatin.

On the chromatin side, the Polycomb component BMI1 is part of the complex that ubiquitinates histone H2A to silence the CDKN2A locus and keep cells cycling, while the deubiquitinase USP16 removes that mark and opposes it, so the balance between them sets how readily a cell exits the cycle.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on transcriptional repression and chromatin-based silencing, the machinery that keeps developmental and proliferative genes switched off until they are needed. Polycomb components are the anchor: BMI1 is a core subunit of the PRC1 ubiquitin ligase complex that marks histone H2A to maintain silencing, while AEBP2 is a zinc-finger accessory factor that helps target the companion PRC2 methyltransferase to chromatin.
